title: Isaiah Bible Quiz - Chapter 16
description: Ten questions on Isaiah 16: lambs for the ruler of the land, a throne in David's tent, Moab's pride, and the withered vine of Sibmah.

questions.text: What does verse 1 say to send for the ruler of the land?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 says, "Send the lambs for the ruler of the land from Selah to the wilderness, to the mountain of the daughter of Zion."

questions.text: What are the daughters of Moab at the fords of the Arnon compared to?
questions.explanation: Verse 2 says that like wandering birds, like a scattered nest, so will the daughters of Moab be at the fords of the Arnon.

questions.text: In whose tent will the throne of verse 5 be established?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says a throne will be established in loving kindness, and one will sit on it in truth, in the tent of David.

questions.text: What have we heard of Moab according to verse 6?
questions.explanation: Verse 6 says, "We have heard of the pride of Moab, that he is very proud," and that his boastings are nothing.

answers.text: Of his wisdom, that he is very wise
Of his wealth, that he is very rich
Of his armies, that they are very strong
Of his pride, that he is very proud

questions.text: For what will the people mourn, utterly stricken?
questions.explanation: Verse 7 says everyone will wail, and you will mourn for the raisin cakes of Kir Hareseth, utterly stricken.

answers.text: The raisin cakes of Kir Hareseth

questions.text: The fields of which place languish along with the vine of Sibmah?
questions.explanation: Verse 8 says the fields of Heshbon languish with the vine of Sibmah, whose branches reached even to Jazer.

questions.text: What does verse 10 say will no longer happen in the vineyards?
questions.explanation: Verse 10 says there will be no singing in the vineyards, and nobody will tread out wine in the presses.

answers.text: No singing and no treading out wine
No gathering of grapes into baskets

questions.text: What does the speaker's heart sound like for Moab?
questions.explanation: Verse 11 says, "my heart sounds like a harp for Moab, and my inward parts for Kir Heres."

questions.text: What happens when Moab comes to his sanctuary to pray?
questions.explanation: Verse 12 says that when Moab wearies himself on the high place and comes to his sanctuary to pray, he will not prevail.

answers.text: He will be heard at last
He will be driven out by priests

questions.text: Within how many years will the glory of Moab be brought into contempt?
questions.explanation: Verse 14 says that within three years, as a worker bound by contract would count them, the glory of Moab shall be brought into contempt.
